name: Commit message quality
description: Judge a single commit message against Conventional Commits and good-practice rules.
state:
fix(auth): refresh expired session tokens before retrying API calls

Clients with a session older than 24h were getting a 401 on the first request after
waking from sleep, because the SDK retried with the stale token. We now check `expires_at`
before each call and refresh proactively when less than 60s remain.

Fixes #4821

follows_conventional_commits.instructions: Does the commit message follow the Conventional Commits format: a header of the form `type(optional scope): description`, with a lowercase type from the standard set?

criteria.true: Header matches `type(scope)?: description` with a known type (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert).
criteria.false: No type prefix, wrong separator, unknown type, or the header is a free-form sentence.

imperative_mood.instructions: Is the summary line (the part after the type prefix) written in the imperative mood, as in 'add X' or 'fix Y', rather than 'added', 'fixes', or 'adding'?

explains_why.instructions: How well does the message explain the motivation for the change, not just what changed?
criteria: No body, or the body restates the subject line.
Mentions a symptom or ticket but not the underlying cause.
Explains the cause and why this approach fixes it.
Explains cause, approach, and trade-offs or alternatives considered.

type.instructions: Which Conventional Commits type best describes this change based on the content of the message (ignore the prefix the author wrote if it contradicts the body)?

criteria.feat: A new feature for the user.
criteria.style: Formatting, whitespace, missing semicolons; no code meaning change.
criteria.refactor: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature.
criteria.chore: Other changes that do not modify src or test files.

pair.label: Adding a body explaining the cause should raise explains_why
